title: Rollout scenario matrix and interaction proposals
content:
Purpose: capture a concise interaction-first proposal for how the Console should present, configure, and preview multi-step rollouts (canary, A/B, multi-variant, and automatic fallback). This doc is intentionally UX-focused — not an exhaustive backend contract — and aims to feed the backlog grooming session on 2026-02-26.

Goals (what users need):
- Product/Platform engineer wants a fast way to create and reason about rollout plans that include: traffic splits, model variant selection, health gates, automatic fallback behaviors, and staged timers.
- Solutions engineers need clear preview sims and a deterministic playback mode to show customers expected behavior.
- SRE/Infra wants embedded policy checks (e.g., quota, region constraints, required model compatibility) surfaced in the UI before commit.

Audience / personas:
- PM / Product engineer (sets experiment & metrics)
- Platform / Solutions engineer (wiring and testing)
- SRE (operational constraints)
- Customer success / SE (demoing to enterprise customers)

High-level interaction model (candidate flow):
1) Create rollout: top-level form with name, description, target route(s), and primary metric(s).
2) Add stages: each stage has a type (canary | A/B variant | ramp | hold), duration (P1M or cron), traffic fraction, model variant(s).
3) Configure gates: attach one or more gates to a stage (metric threshold, error rate, latency p95, quality regression on eval set).
4) Define fallback policies: (a) immediate fallback to baseline; (b) rollback to previously-stable variant; (c) automatic gradual roll-to-zero with alert.
5) Dry-run / Simulation: run traffic simulation with historical distribution or synthetic workload and visualize expected metric trajectories + guardrail triggers.
6) Launch (with optional canary preview in 'staging' namespace).

Wireframe writeups (panels & key interactions):
- Left column: route selector + quick health summary for selected route.
- Middle canvas: stage timeline (horizontal) where each stage is a color-coded block. Drag to reorder, click to edit stage properties. Inline badges show gate count, duration, traffic %.
- Right rail: properties for selected stage (model dropdown, traffic slider, gates list). Advanced collapse: rollout-level policies (circuit-breaker settings, cross-region fallback).
- Top bar: commit button (Commit & Launch), Save draft, Simulate. Commit triggers preflight checks (quota, model binary availability).

Simulation mode specifics:
- Option to seed simulation from last 24h traffic or upload CSV.
- Visuals: metric lines with shaded confidence intervals; vertical markers where gates would evaluate.
- Synthetic failure toggles: spike latency, token cost budget breach, KV-cache miss spike. These toggle expected fallback behaviors to preview consequences.

Fallback policy editor (new focused panel):
- Simple templates: "Immediate fallback", "Graceful ramp-down to baseline", "Fallback to model variant X", "Notify + hold".
- Advanced: sequence of actions on trigger (alert -> 3m hold -> rollback -> escalate). Actions have delays and can be chained.
- UI shows the rollback path as a reversed timeline so operators can see safe states.

Rollout scenario matrix (design-time checklist):
- Canary small (1-5% traffic) + metric gate (latency p95 < 250ms) -> expect: quick detection, immediate fallback on violation.
- A/B equal split (50/50 model compare) + quality score gate -> expect: statistical significance window defined (min sample N).
- Multi-variant gradual ramp (0 -> 100 over 3 stages) + cost gate -> expect: staged throttling when token unit cost exceeds budget.
- Region fallback (primary region outage) -> expect: auto-route to replica region and degrade to lower-capacity variant if needed.

Backlog items (proposed priorities):
- P0: Stage timeline canvas + stage edit panel (RINF-3310) — UX + minimal API for creating stages.
- P0: Preflight checks modal with live hints for required inventory (models, GPUs, quotas).
- P1: Simulation engine UI + CSV seeding + synthetic failure toggles.
- P1: Basic fallback templates + UI to attach to stage.
- P2: Advanced fallback action chains + audit trail entries.
- P2: Cross-org policies (enforce SRE policy, auto-approve for trusted teams).

Edge cases & constraints called out by SRE/Infra:
- Model variant compatibility: when using KV-cache pinned variants, mixing incompatible quantization may cause fallback to baseline; UI must warn when selecting incompatible pairs.
- Billing impact: simulation should show estimated token spend and projected cost delta; require explicit checkbox for high-cost rollouts.
- Offline/private deployments: some automation (e.g., auto-fallback to regional replica) not available in Private mode; surface a disabled state and provide manual instructions.

Open questions (for grooming session):
- Gate evaluation cadence: should gates evaluate at end of stage only, or continuously during stage with immediate rollback option?
- Statistical significance handling: do we surface p-value and confidence intervals or keep a simplified "min-samples + delta" model?
- Role boundaries: who is allowed to create automatic fallback sequences? RBAC implications.

Design notes / microcopy drafts:
- Commit button -> "Commit rollout and start canary" (with tooltip: reversible until final stage completes).
- Gate failure toast -> "Gate failed: automatic fallback executed to [variant]. Click to inspect replay."
- Simulation header -> "Dry run: no traffic changed. This sim predicts effect given seed data."

Accessibility & copy considerations:
- Use color + pattern fills on timeline blocks to support colorblind users.
- Ensure keyboard-first editing for stage properties.

Appendix: quick sketch ideas (copyable to figma)
- Canvas coordinate system: time left-to-right, stages snap to day/hour grid.
- Inline mini-graphs inside each stage block showing metric preview (tiny sparkline).
- Right-click stage -> quick actions: pause, duplicate, open-simulation, export-stage-config.

Next steps (action items):
- [Ava] finalize draft and add basic figma frames by 2026-02-02.
- [Ravi] scope backend APIs required for stage creation + preflight by 2026-02-09.
- [Sofia] prototype simulation UI (mock data) and bring to grooming on 2026-02-26.
- Add a follow-up JIRA task to define gate metric schemas (RINF-3342).

Notes to reviewers: please read the "Open questions" section and add stance comments inline in Confluence page linked above. The goal for the grooming session is to convert the P0 items into sprint-ready tickets and to agree on gate evaluation cadence.

Unresolved / TODO during grooming:
- Decide if automatic fallback should be allowed for customer-managed Private deployments.
- Finalize the set of canned fallback templates.

End of doc.
